title: Github Dorks & Leaks

Github Dorks & Leaks

Tools to find secrets in git repos and file system

  • TruffleHog
  • Gitleaks
  • Nosey Parker (archived; replaced by Titus)
  • ggshield
  • RExpository
  • detect-secrets
  • gitGraber
  • shhgit (unmaintained)
  • github-dorks
  • gitrob (archived)
  • git-all-secrets (archived)
  • git-secrets
  • gittyleaks
  • GitDorker

Notes - TruffleHog v3 can verify many credentials live and scan GitHub orgs, issues/PRs, gists, and wikis. Example: trufflehog github --org <ORG> --results=verified.[2][13] - Gitleaks scans Git repositories, directories, and archives. Use gitleaks git -v --log-opts="--all" <repo> for history, gitleaks dir -v <path> for directories, and --max-archive-depth 1 to inspect archives.[6] - Nosey Parker is archived and replaced by Titus. Existing installations still support noseyparker scan --datastore np.db <path|repo> followed by noseyparker report --datastore np.db.[7][8] - ggshield (GitGuardian CLI) scans files, repositories, and Docker images and integrates with local or CI workflows: ggshield secret scan repo <path-or-url>.[9]

Where secrets commonly leak in GitHub

  • GitHub Code Search indexes the default branch only; inspect non-default branches directly or clone them.[4]
  • Full git history and other branches/tags (clone and scan with gitleaks/trufflehog; GitHub search covers only indexed content).[4][6]
  • Issues, pull requests, comments, and descriptions (TruffleHog's GitHub source supports these via flags such as --issue-comments and --pr-comments).[2]
  • Actions workflow logs and artifacts (read access allows them to be viewed or downloaded, and secret redaction is not guaranteed).[11][12]
  • Wikis and release assets.
  • Gists (search with tooling or the UI; some tools can include gists).[2][13]

Gotchas - GitHub's Code Search UI supports regex, while the REST/API path (including gh search code) uses the legacy engine and does not expose regex features. Prefer the UI for regex queries.[3][5] - GitHub search excludes files above its documented size limit and is not exhaustive. To be thorough, clone and scan locally with a secrets scanner.[4]

Programmatic org-wide scanning

  • TruffleHog (GitHub source).[2][13] 
    export GITHUB_TOKEN=<token>
trufflehog github --org Target --results=verified \
  --include-wikis --issue-comments --pr-comments --gist-comments
  • Gitleaks over all org repos (clone shallow and scan with gitleaks dir).[6] 
    gh repo list Target --limit 1000 --json nameWithOwner,url \
| jq -r '.[].url' | while read -r r; do
  tmp=$(mktemp -d); git clone --depth 1 "$r" "$tmp" && \
  gitleaks dir -v "$tmp" || true; rm -rf "$tmp";
done
  • Nosey Parker over a mono checkout (for existing installations).[7] 
    # after cloning many repos beneath ./org
noseyparker scan --datastore np.db org/ && noseyparker report --datastore np.db
  • ggshield quick scans.[9] 
    # current working tree
ggshield secret scan path -r .
# full git history of a repo
ggshield secret scan repo <path-or-url>

Tip: For git history, prefer scanners that parse git log -p --all to catch removed secrets.[6]

Pull-request refs and Gist revision history

Normal clones do not fetch GitHub's refs/pull/<number>/head refs, so git log --all misses commits reachable only through those refs until you fetch them.[14][17] PR refs can expose unmerged commits even after a contributor deletes their fork.[15] Rewriting branch history alone may leave sensitive commits reachable through PR references.[16]

In a full clone, fetch a selected PR head before scanning, or use the wildcard refspec for all advertised PR heads when the extra download is justified.[17][18] Gitleaks scans local commit patches with git log -p, so rerun it after fetching the refs.[6]

git fetch origin 'refs/pull/123/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/123'
# Or fetch every advertised PR head:
git fetch origin '+refs/pull/*/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/*'
gitleaks git -v --log-opts="--all" .

A Gist also has a Git history, so checking only its current files can miss a credential removed in a later revision.[19] For an in-scope public Gist, clone its Git repository and scan the revisions.[19][6]

git clone https://gist.github.com/GIST_ID.git
gitleaks git -v --log-opts="--all" GIST_ID
